subject: Post-call: Technical deep-dive recap — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Technical deep-dive recap — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our technical deep-dive: 

Key pain points you called out:
- User-facing generation latency spikes during peak traffic (critical for chat feature).
- Large variance in throughput for batch backend jobs (summary/embedding pipelines).
- Limited visibility into per-route token costs and per-request tracing.

Goals we discussed:
- Achieve 95th percentile tail latency <= 450ms for 512-token chat requests under expected peak load (~120 rps).
- Sustained throughput of 2,500 tok/s for nightly batch summarization (with predictable cost).
- End-to-end tracing + token-level cost breakdown for three high-volume routes.

Technical constraints / model requirements:
- Production model: transformer-based causal model (approx 13B) with KV-cache usage and occasional long-context (>2k tokens) requests.
- Want to evaluate 8-bit quantized variants and a Quantized-LLM baseline for throughput.
- Data residency: traffic originating in US with optional EU region failover.

Proposed deployment topology (high-level):
1) Hosted Redwood API for initial validation (canary traffic for chat route).
2) Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) for production chat route to guarantee latency SLOs.
3) Private VPC connectors for batch pipelines to meet ingress egress policies (if/when procurement completes).

Immediate next steps (owners and timeline):
- Redwood: share SLO proposal + topology diagram (attached) — Marissa — by EOD today.
- ACME: provide representative sample of peak traffic traces and current p95/p99 numbers — Samir — by Mon 6/15.
- SE deep bench: run quantized 13B baseline latency/throughput pass and share bench artifacts — Aditya/Ethan — by Fri 6/12.

Attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (topology diagrams and suggested instance types).

If any of the summary points are off, flag them here and I'll update. Otherwise we can lock calendar for a follow-up on Tue 6/16 to review bench results and finalize a canary plan.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Technical deep-dive recap — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming a few specifics from ACME side: 

- For chat route latency: our current p95 is ~380ms, p99 ~1.1s in production during peak windows (US-east). The 450ms p95 target is aggressive but aligns with our product goals.
- Batch throughput: our nightly window processes ~600k documents; throughput target of 2,500 tok/s would reduce run time but we'd also want to ensure cost per run doesn't exceed our current spend by more than 20%.
- Model requirements: we are open to a 13B quantized candidate; we also want a fallback smaller 6B for emergency graceful degradation.

Action items from ACME:
- I'll upload a zipped slice of traffic traces and the current KPI sheet (will post link to platform@acme.com).
- Can you and Aditya include expected instance types and cost delta between hosted canary and Dedicated reserved pool in the SLO doc?

Thanks — Samir

Subject: RE: Post-call: Technical deep-dive recap — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Samir — quick note from the SE bench work we kicked off this morning. Summary so far: 

- Environment: 13B causal model (FP16 baseline + 8-bit quant) on g4dn (probe) and dedicated A10G-equivalent nodes in our infra lab.
- Initial single-request median latency for 512-token prompt (FP16): ~220ms on A10G-equivalent, 340ms on g4dn.
- 8-bit quantized run shows ~1.6x throughput improvement in batch workloads with ~6-8% generation quality delta (we'll attach eval examples).
- Memory: KV cache for long-context increases memory by ~40% for >2k sequences; suggest Dedicated pool with 48GB GPU RAM or split routing for long-context requests.

Attached: latency-benchmark.png (summary chart), acme_kpi_sheet.xlsx (template to align costs), redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (updated with instance/cost notes).

Questions for ACME:
- Can you confirm expected 95th percentile traffic arrival rate over a 1-minute window during peak? We used 120 rps as discussed but want a 1-min burst profile.
- For fallback model: is a 6B with lower context acceptable for degraded sessions, or do you need full-context parity?

I can join the Tue 6/16 follow-up and walk through the bench artifacts.
—Aditya
Senior Field SE | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

See you Tue 6/16 — Samir
